scope.chapterTitle: Cell Structure, Epithelia, Glands & Connective Tissue

marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q011.takeaway: Stratified squamous epithelium has deeper columnar cells and progressively flatter superficial cells.
marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q011.displayText: The multilayered epithelium that consists of deeper columnar cells and a surface layer of flat cells is stratified squamous epithelium. Stratified epithelia include stratified squamous, stratified cuboidal/columnar, and transitional epithelium. In stratified squamous epithelium the deepest layer is columnar, above which are layers of cuboidal cells; toward the surface the cells become increasingly flattened. It may be keratinized or non-keratinized. Stratified cuboidal/columnar epithelium consists of two or more layers of cuboidal or columnar cells respectively; salivary-gland ducts are illustrated. Transitional epithelium is a specialized epithelium lining most of the urinary tract (urothelium). Its deepest layer is columnar or cuboidal, middle cells are polyhedral or pear-shaped, and surface cells are large polypoid/dome/umbrella-shaped cells that flatten on stretching. This apparent transition gives the epithelium its name.

rationales.a: Pseudostratified columnar epithelium is a single layer whose nuclei lie at different heights; it is not a true multilayered epithelium with flattening at the surface.
rationales.b: Stratified columnar epithelium has columnar surface cells, whereas the described epithelium has flat superficial cells.
rationales.c: Pseudostratified epithelium is not the multilayered epithelial type described; this is stratified squamous epithelium.

marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q012.takeaway: The deepest layer of stratified squamous epithelium is columnar.
marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q012.displayText: The basal layer of stratified squamous epithelium is composed of columnar cells. Stratified squamous epithelium has columnar cells in the deepest layer, polygonal cells in the middle layers, and flattened squamous cells in the superficial layers. It may be keratinized or non-keratinized.

rationales.a: Cuboidal cells are not the source-described deepest layer; the basal cells are columnar.
rationales.c: Squamous cells form the superficial layers after flattening, not the basal layer.
rationales.d: Transitional epithelium is a distinct urothelium with specialized surface cells, not the basal layer type asked here.

marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q013.takeaway: The cornea is lined by stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium.
marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q013.displayText: The cornea is lined by stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium. The cornea is made up of five layers; its outermost layer is non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium (corneal epithelium), which can regenerate rapidly after damage. A non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium of the esophagus is shown as a histological comparison.

rationales.a: Simple squamous epithelium is one cell layer thick; the corneal epithelium is stratified.
rationales.b: Keratinized stratified squamous epithelium characterizes skin, whereas the corneal surface is non-keratinized.
rationales.d: The cornea is not lined by pseudostratified columnar epithelium; its outer layer is stratified squamous non-keratinized.

marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q014.takeaway: Sebaceous gland ducts have keratinized stratified squamous lining, unlike the compared stratified cuboidal ducts.
marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q014.displayText: The ducts of the sebaceous gland are lined by keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, whereas the ducts of sweat glands, salivary glands and exocrine pancreas are lined by stratified cuboidal epithelium.

rationales.a: Sweat gland ducts are lined by stratified cuboidal epithelium in the source comparison, matching the other listed exocrine ducts.
rationales.c: Salivary gland ducts are lined by stratified cuboidal epithelium in the source comparison.
rationales.d: Exocrine pancreatic ducts are grouped with stratified cuboidal ducts in the source comparison.

marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q015.takeaway: Transitional epithelium (urothelium) lines the urinary bladder and much of the urinary tract.
marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q015.displayText: The epithelium shown is transitional epithelium and is present in the urinary bladder. Transitional epithelium is specialized epithelium lining most of the urinary tract and is also called urothelium. Its deepest layer consists of columnar or cuboidal cells, the middle layer of polyhedral or pear-shaped cells, and the surface layer of large polypoid, dome-shaped or umbrella-shaped cells. On stretching to accommodate urine, the surface cells flatten. It is present in collecting ducts, renal pelvis and calyces, ureter, urinary bladder, and the pre-prostatic and prostatic parts of the urethra.

rationales.a: The duodenum is lined by intestinal epithelium, not urothelium.
rationales.b: The common bile duct is not part of the urinary tract and does not have transitional lining.
rationales.c: Skin has keratinized stratified squamous epithelium rather than transitional epithelium.

marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q016.takeaway: The loop of Henle contains squamous and cuboidal epithelial segments.
marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q016.displayText: The loop of Henle, also called ansa nephroni, is lined by both squamous and cuboidal epithelium in different parts. Tubular epithelial cells grow progressively taller through the nephron segment until cells in the collecting duct form a simple columnar epithelium. The source illustrates a kidney cross-section showing thin and thick loops of Henle.

rationales.a: The loop contains squamous and cuboidal segments, not a columnar segment as stated here.
rationales.b: Columnar cells characterize the collecting duct in the source comparison; the loop has squamous and cuboidal regions.
rationales.d: The loop has both thin squamous and thicker cuboidal regions, so it is not squamous throughout.

marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q017.takeaway: Collecting ducts lack microvilli; the listed absorptive epithelia possess them.
marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q017.displayText: Microvilli are absent in collecting ducts, which are lined by simple columnar epithelium without microvilli. Simple cuboidal or columnar epithelium may show specializations. Microvilli are long finger-like projections that increase absorptive surface area; regularly arranged long microvilli create a striated appearance, whereas irregular arrangement creates a brush border. They are present in small intestine (striated microvilli), gall bladder (brush-border microvilli), and proximal convoluted tubule (brush-border microvilli). Stereocilia are long, branching, non-motile microvilli (stereovilli), found in epididymis and cochlear/vestibular receptor cells. Cilia are hair-like projections concerned with movement and occur in the respiratory tract except lower pharynx and vocal folds, tympanic cavity and auditory tube, uterine tube, and efferent ductules of testis. Columnar cells may also be specialized for secretion, as in mucin-secreting and chief cells of gastric epithelium.
emphasis: Microvilli are absent in collecting ducts

rationales.a: Small-intestinal epithelium has microvilli that increase absorptive surface area.
rationales.c: Proximal convoluted tubules have brush-border microvilli; collecting ducts are the listed site without them.

marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q018.takeaway: Sweat glands are simple coiled tubular glands.
marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q018.displayText: Sweat glands are simple coiled tubular glands.

rationales.a: Simple tubular describes a straight unbranched gland; sweat glands are coiled.
rationales.c: Compound tubular glands have branching secretory units, unlike the simple coiled sweat gland.
rationales.d: Compound acinar glands have branched sac-like secretory units, not the tubular sweat-gland form.

marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q019.takeaway: Sebaceous glands are holocrine: secretion is released by disintegration of the whole cell.
marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q019.displayText: The sebaceous gland is a holocrine gland. Exocrine glands are classified by mode of secretion. Merocrine (eccrine/epicrine) glands release secretion by exocytosis while the cell remains intact; examples include eccrine sweat glands, salivary glands, exocrine pancreas, and secretion of milk protein casein by mammary glands. Holocrine glands discharge secretion by disintegration of the entire cell, as in sebaceous glands. In apocrine glands the apical part of the cell is shed to discharge secretion; examples include sweat glands in axilla and anogenital regions and secretion of milk fat by mammary glands.

rationales.a: Eccrine sweat glands secrete by merocrine exocytosis while the cell remains intact.
rationales.b: Mammary secretion is not wholly holocrine: milk protein is merocrine and milk fat may be apocrine.
rationales.c: The exocrine pancreas releases secretion by merocrine exocytosis, not destruction of the entire cell.

marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q020.takeaway: In the source image, option B is a sebaceous gland, whose secretion is holocrine.
marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q020.displayText: Image B represents a sebaceous gland, a holocrine gland. Holocrine secretions are produced in the cytoplasm and released by rupture of the plasma membrane, which destroys the cell and releases the product into the lumen. Examples include sebaceous glands of skin and Meibomian glands of the eyelid. Image A shows sweat glands (eccrine/merocrine; glands remain intact), image C shows mammary gland (apocrine; apical part sheds), and image D shows ceruminous gland (apocrine).
emphasis: Image B represents a sebaceous gland

rationales.a: The source identifies image A as sweat gland, which secretes by the merocrine mode rather than holocrine cell disintegration.
rationales.c: The source identifies image C as mammary gland; its secretion is described as apocrine for milk fat, not holocrine.
rationales.d: The source identifies image D as ceruminous gland, an apocrine gland rather than the holocrine sebaceous gland.

marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q021.takeaway: Mucous acini lack zymogen granules; those granules are characteristic of serous acini.
marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q021.displayText: Zymogen granules are present in serous acini, whereas mucous acini contain mucoid material. Serous acini have triangular cells with rounded nuclei at the base, indistinct cell boundaries, and stain darkly with H&E; parotid gland is an example. Mucous acini have tall cells with flat nuclei at the base, distinct cell boundaries, and stain lightly/appear empty with H&E; sublingual gland is an example.
emphasis: Zymogen granules are present in serous acini

rationales.a: Mucous acini do have tall cells with flattened basal nuclei.
rationales.c: Mucous acini stain lightly and may appear empty with H&E, unlike the darkly stained serous acini.
rationales.d: Mucous acini have distinct cell boundaries; indistinct boundaries describe serous acini.

marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q022.takeaway: Reticular fibers are argyrophilic and stain black with silver impregnation.
marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q022.displayText: Reticular fibers are stained black with the silver impregnation method. They are also called argentophil fibers because of their affinity for silver salts. The three main connective-tissue fiber types are collagen, reticular and elastic fibers. The source compares staining characteristics and shows reticular fibers black with silver impregnation, collagen fibers blue and muscle fibers red with Masson trichrome stain, and elastic fibers black with Verhoeff-Van Gieson stain.
emphasis: Reticular fibers are stained black with the silver impregnation method

rationales.a: Type I collagen is distinguished from reticular fibers; the source associates black silver impregnation with reticular fibers.
rationales.b: Elastic fibers stain black with Verhoeff–Van Gieson in the source comparison, not by silver impregnation.
rationales.d: Type II collagen is not the fiber identified by the source as black with silver impregnation.

marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q023.takeaway: Mast cells are connective-tissue cells of immune origin, not intrinsic resident connective-tissue cells.
marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q023.displayText: Mast cells are not part of the intrinsic component of connective tissue. Cells intrinsic to connective tissue include fibroblasts, undifferentiated mesenchymal cells, pigment cells and adipocytes. Cells that belong to the immune system include macrophages (histiocytes), mast cells, lymphocytes, plasma cells, monocytes and eosinophils.
emphasis: Mast cells are not part of the intrinsic component

rationales.a: Fibroblasts are intrinsic connective-tissue cells that produce and maintain extracellular matrix.
rationales.b: Adipocytes are listed among intrinsic connective-tissue cells.
rationales.d: Pigment cells are included among intrinsic connective-tissue components in the source classification.

marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q024.takeaway: Sudan III and IV stain adipose tissue.
marrow__ANAT_CH11_Q024.displayText: Sudan III and Sudan IV dyes are used for staining adipose tissue. During routine slide preparation, tissues are treated with fat solvents such as xylene or benzene that dissolve fat; therefore fat cells appear as rounded empty spaces in such preparations.
emphasis: Sudan III and Sudan IV dyes

rationales.a: Sudan III and IV are fat stains; elastic tissue is not their target in this item.
rationales.b: Mucoid tissue is not the lipid-rich tissue stained by Sudan dyes.
rationales.d: Reticular tissue is identified by reticular fibers and silver affinity, whereas Sudan dyes stain adipose tissue.
